Message Performance

What we actually said, and which of it earned attention — 2025-10-07 to 2026-10-07
Last updated October 07, 2026 at 09:11 AM • refreshed daily by the analytics pipeline
Read this first. ROAS on this page is platform-attributed — Meta's and Google's own reported conversion value divided by spend. It is not Shopify truth and it is not incremental. Use it to rank pillars against each other, never as a profitability number. Prospecting and retargeting are never pooled: retargeting ROAS runs 4–7× against prospecting's 0.5–1.0×, so a blended figure just ranks pillars by how much retargeting they happened to receive. Any figure below $1,000 of spend inside one funnel is withheld as thin.

The verdict

one card per pillar · ranked by prospecting CTR, not by spend
Spend is the input; attention is the outcome — so the cards are ordered by how well each pillar earned a click from a cold audience. Click any card to open its sub-pillars and the individual creative concepts inside it. Prospecting shows impressions and reach; reach is the honest denominator for how many distinct people heard the message.

Google — campaign level

no creative read · no funnel split · never summed with Meta
Google is largely a product and intent channel, not a message channel. Campaign names carry a theme, but there is no per-ad creative data and PMax campaigns have no reliable funnel label — so there is no TOF/retargeting split here and these rows cannot be compared like-for-like with the Meta cards. The date filter applies here; the ad-type filter does not, because there is no creative record to read a type from. Data through 2026-10-07.

Unlabeled ads

the worklist behind the coverage figure · 121 ads · $18,285 over the full window
Every ad here is spend this page cannot read a message off. It is still inside every denominator above — nothing is dropped — but it contributes no signal to any pillar, so each dollar of it is a dollar we cannot learn from. The three reasons below need three different people to do three different things, which is why they are split rather than pooled into the single coverage figure. This panel follows the date and ad-type filters; the full-window backlog is restated beside the selection so narrowing can never make it look smaller than it is.
Not one ad in this window is labelled from its own name — every label on this page came from a hand-classified file. The naming standard is the only permanent fix: an ad named to the standard classifies itself on the night it first spends, with no backlog and nobody in the loop. Everything else is a hand-classified file, and a file classified by hand is a snapshot that goes stale the day the next ad launches.

Sources. Meta: raw_meta_ad_insights_daily (per-ad daily). Google: raw_google_ads_campaigns (per-campaign daily). Both in the analytics database, refreshed by the nightly pipeline.
Labels. Taxonomy v2 — the Pillars, ratified 2026-09-11 — the top axis is a Pillar and the second level a Sub-pillar; Caffeine Free was split out of Quitting Coffee. Content owned by AdSmith, schema by AgentSmith. Each ad is resolved from its own name first (per the ratified naming standard) and only then from the hand-classified concept file, so the page gets easier as the naming standard lands rather than staying manual forever.
Funnel. Derived from the campaign name first and the ad-set name only as a fallback — one ad set currently sits under both a COLD and a Retargeting campaign, so ad-set-only derivation mis-buckets spend.
Reach is summed across days. It is not a de-duplicated count of unique people over the whole period; a person reached in two different weeks is counted twice. Use it to compare pillars against each other, not as an audience size.
Meta totals (for the filter you have selected). $258,369 across 9 pillar buckets — prospecting $212,756, retargeting $45,612. Prospecting CTR averages 1.88% across the selection; the UNDERSPENT flag fires at 1.4× that on under 4% of prospecting spend, and is recomputed against the selection rather than against the year.
Creative type. Meta's own field on the ad. It is absent on a slice of daily rows, so a null is back-filled from the same ad's other days — ad id first, then ad name, both verified to carry no conflicting type in this window. Whatever is still null is reported as type not reported and never folded into Image.
